title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on How to Impose Combined Punishment for Multiple Crimes in Cases Where Some Crimes Are Punishable by Life Imprisonment or Above
keywords_en: cases involving life imprisonment or above
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on How to Impose Concurrent Punishment for Multiple Crimes Where Life Imprisonment or Above Is Sentenced

Fa (Xing Yi) Fa [1987] No. 16

To all Higher People's Courts and Intermediate People's Courts in various localities nationwide, the Military Courts of the People's Liberation Army, the Military Courts of major units, all Railway Transport Intermediate Courts, and all Maritime Courts:

Regarding cases where one or more of multiple crimes should be sentenced to life imprisonment or the death penalty (including the death penalty with a two-year reprieve, hereinafter the same), the practices of courts in various localities are not entirely consistent. Some courts separately sentence each crime before determining the punishment to be executed; others list the charges without separately sentencing and only impose the highest punishment among them. Based on trial practice, if separate sentencing is not conducted for such cases, it is impossible to discern how each crime has been sentenced, which may not only affect the defendant's exercise of the right to appeal but also cause difficulties for higher courts in reviewing whether the original sentence is appropriate. For this reason, notice is hereby given as follows: In accordance with the provisions of Article 64 of the Criminal Law, henceforth, when a defendant is convicted of multiple crimes, and one or more of those crimes should be sentenced to life imprisonment or the death penalty, each crime shall be sentenced separately, and then the highest punishment among them shall be executed. It is expected that all courts shall comply accordingly.

June 26, 1987
